methods.name: merge_adapter
methods.signature: merge_adapter(adapter_names: list[str] | None = None, safe_merge: bool = False)
methods.summary: Fold adapter updates into their base weights, each module's layers lowest first.
methods.extended:
A layer's update is computed from the weight the layers beneath it have left, so the
order is the stack's, and a merge that would fold an update under a layer that
transforms it differently is refused before any weight is written.  A layer
standing on others folds into the user's module, so what is left unmerged beneath a
merged layer must be a sum of terms that commutes with it: refused are the merge of a
layer while a lower layer keeps adapters in use (its active adapters not merged, now
or before), and of a lower layer after a higher one has been merged, unless both
layers add a term to the output (LoRA, LoHa, LoKr, AdaLoRA, SHiRA); a layer above a
merged one may stay as it is.  A layer merged for some of its own adapters goes on
applying the others, as in a single method's model, and refuses the splits that method
cannot reproduce (`_BaseTuner.merge_adapter`).

parameters.name: adapter_names
parameters.description: Adapters to merge; the active ones by default.

parameters.name: safe_merge
parameters.description: Check every merged weight for NaN / inf before writing any.

raises.description: A base weight is shared with another module, or the adapter is disabled.

A name is not one of the model's adapters, the merge would fold a layer's update
under a layer that transforms it or leave a layer unable to apply what stays
unmerged, or `safe_merge` found a non-finite merged weight.

methods.name: active_adapters
methods.summary: The adapters the forward pass applies, as a list.

methods.name: add_adapter
methods.summary: Add an adapter beside the ones the model holds.
methods.extended:
The new adapter starts frozen and inactive: the forward pass keeps
applying the adapters it applied, and every parameter keeps the
`requires_grad` it had.  `set_adapter` switches to it.  A
module an earlier adapter already wraps takes the new one beside
it; any other target is wrapped.  The model is left as it was if
the adapter cannot be added.

parameters.name: adapter_name
parameters.description: Name of the new adapter; unique among the model's adapters.

parameters.name: config
parameters.description: What to adapt and how — the config class of this tuner's method.

raises.description:
The name is taken or malformed, the config is another
method's, no module matches it, or it cannot sit beside the
adapters held (two adapters training biases).

methods.name: set_adapter
methods.signature: set_adapter(adapter_name: str | list[str], inference_mode: bool = False)
methods.summary: Apply the named adapter(s) in the forward pass, and train exactly those.
methods.extended:
Every other adapter is frozen; the activated ones train unless
`inference_mode`.  A merged layer is unmerged first.  Layers that
hold none of the named adapters run their base alone.  The
parameters `bias` makes trainable follow the adapter that asked
for them.

parameters.name: adapter_name
parameters.description: The adapter, or adapters, to apply.

parameters.name: inference_mode
parameters.description: Freeze the activated adapters too.

raises.description:
A name is not one of the model's adapters, or two named
adapters train the same `modules_to_save` module.

methods.name: set_requires_grad
methods.signature: set_requires_grad(adapter_names: str | Sequence[str], requires_grad: bool = True)
methods.summary: Enable or disable gradients on the parameters of the named adapter(s).

raises.description: A name is not one of the model's adapters.

methods.name: delete_adapter
methods.summary: Remove an adapter: its parameters, its config, its `modules_to_save` copies.
methods.extended:
If it was active, the adapters still active stay so; when none
remain the first of the others (by name) takes over, with a
warning, and trains.  Deleting the last adapter leaves the layers
in the model, applying nothing; `unload()` removes them.

raises.description: The adapter does not exist, or it is merged — unmerge first.

methods.name: forward
methods.summary: Call the adapted model; its adapter layers do their work inside the call.

methods.name: unmerge_adapter
methods.summary: Take every merged adapter update back out of its base weight.

methods.name: merge_and_unload
methods.signature: merge_and_unload(progressbar: bool = False, safe_merge: bool = False, adapter_names: list[str] | None = None)
methods.summary: Merge the adapters into the base weights and return the plain model.
methods.extended:
Each adapter layer is replaced by its merged base module — the base
model's own module, holding its own `Parameter` objects — and each
`modules_to_save` entry by the active adapter's trained copy (the
original when that adapter has none).  Adapters not merged are
dropped with their layers.  Every base parameter gets back the
`requires_grad` it had before injection.

parameters.name: progressbar
parameters.description: Accepted for the reference's signature; there is no progress bar.

parameters.name: safe_merge
parameters.description: Check every merged weight for NaN / inf before writing any.

parameters.name: adapter_names
parameters.description: Adapters to merge; the active ones by default.

returns.description: The model, merged, with no adapter layer left in it.

raises.description:
A base weight is shared with another module, or a
`modules_to_save` module shared one (its trained copy would
break the tie).

methods.name: unload
methods.summary: Remove every adapter without merging and return the original model.
methods.extended:
Every adapter layer is replaced by the module it wrapped (a merged
one is unmerged first), every `modules_to_save` entry by its
original module, and every base parameter gets back the
`requires_grad` it had before injection.

methods.name: disable_adapter_layers
methods.summary: Run the base model alone: adapter updates off, original `modules_to_save`.

methods.name: supports_lora_conversion
methods.summary: Whether every adapted layer in this tuner supports conversion to LoRA.

members.summary: A model holding adapters of several methods, their layers stacked on each module.
members.extended:
The first adapter of a method puts that method's layer on the module it targets; the layers of
later methods stand on it, so the forward pass runs the layers lowest first.  A method that
already has a layer on a module gets its further adapters in that layer.  `set_adapter`
names the adapters in use, of any methods; a layer holding none of them passes its input
through to the layer beneath.  Merging folds each module's layers into its weight lowest
first, and `unmerge_adapter` takes them out highest first.

Only methods declared mixable (`mixed=True` in the tuner's class statement) take part.
A layer class stands on another method's layer only if it declares so, so the adapters that
read the base weight (HiRA, DoRA) are the lowest in a stack, and a method that computes from
the weight (BOFT, HRA, MiSS) takes a module alone.  Adding an adapter that cannot sit where
it would land raises `ValueError` and leaves the model as it was.

AdaLoRA takes part for inference: the host does not drive its rank allocator or its
orthogonality loss, which belong to `AdaLoraModel`.  Adapters of methods that train a
shared table (VeRA) or hold one adapter at a time (prompt learning) are not mixable.

parameters.name: model
parameters.description: The model to adapt; it must hold no adapters yet.

parameters.name: peft_config
parameters.description: The first adapter's config: any mixable method's.

parameters.name: adapter_name
parameters.description: Name of the first adapter.

parameters.name: low_cpu_mem_usage
parameters.description: As in `lucid.peft.LoraModel`.

parameters.name: state_dict
parameters.description: As in `lucid.peft.LoraModel`.

raises.description:
The method is not mixable, the model already holds adapters, or the adapter cannot be
applied (no module matches, or a layer cannot stand where this one would).

examples:
>>> import lucid.nn as nn
>>> from lucid.peft import LoHaConfig, LoraConfig
>>> from lucid.peft.tuners import MixedModel
>>> net = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(8, 8), nn.ReLU(), nn.Linear(8, 2))
>>> mixed = MixedModel(net, LoraConfig(r=2, target_modules=["0"]), "lora")
>>> mixed.add_adapter("loha", LoHaConfig(r=2, target_modules=["0"]))
>>> type(net[0]).__module__.rsplit(".", 2)[-2:], type(net[0].base_layer).__module__.rsplit(".", 2)[-2:]
(['loha', '_layer'], ['lora', '_layer'])
>>> mixed.set_adapter(["lora", "loha"])
>>> mixed.active_adapters
['lora', 'loha']
>>> mixed.unload() is net, type(net[0]) is nn.Linear
(True, True)

summary: `lucid.peft.tuners` — one sub-package per parameter-efficient method, 46 in all.
extended:
A method is a config class, a tuner (the model-level host that injects, switches, merges and
saves its adapters) and, for the methods that adapt weights, the layer types that wrap the
modules it targets.  Each sub-package holds those layer types together with the method's
config and tuner, registered by `PeftType` on import; the configs and tuners are also exported
from `lucid.peft`, which is where `get_peft_model` and `PeftModel.from_pretrained` live.
The methods, by family:

* **LoRA family** — a low-rank update beside each frozen weight: `lora` (LoRA, with DoRA, rsLoRA
  and PiSSA / OLoRA starts) and `adalora` (AdaLoRA, rank allocated per layer during training).
* **Orthogonal family** — a rotation of each layer's input space instead of an addition to its
  weight: `oft` (block-diagonal Cayley rotations), `boft` (their butterfly factorisation) and
  `hra` (a chain of Householder reflections).
* **LyCORIS family** — a weight-shaped update from a structured factorisation: `loha` (a Hadamard
  product of low-rank products) and `lokr` (a Kronecker product).
* **Prompt learning** — an input learned instead of a weight, with no layer added to the model:
  `prompt_tuning` (virtual tokens in front of the embeddings), `prefix_tuning` (virtual keys and
  values in every attention layer), `p_tuning` (tokens an MLP or LSTM produces),
  `multitask_prompt_tuning` (one prompt shared across tasks, scaled per task) and `cpt` (a
  prompt of in-context examples with a bounded learned offset and its own loss).
* **Shared-table tuners** — one set of tensors for the whole model, held once by the tuner, with a
  few parameters per layer: `vera` (shared random projections, two vectors per layer),
  `randlora` (shared random bases, a full-rank update) and `vblora` (a shared vector bank).
* **Structured and sparse updates** — a weight update with a fixed structure other than low rank:
  `fourierft` (a few frequency coefficients), `c3a` (block-circulant blocks), `miss` (shared
  matrix shards), `bone` (the method MiSS replaced, kept to read old adapter files) and `shira`
  (a sparse subset of the weight itself).
* **Routing and mixing** — several low-rank adapters combined per task or per token: `poly`
  (low-rank skills mixed by a per-task router) and `xlora` (LoRA experts weighed per token by a
  classifier on the hidden states).
* **Adaption prompts** — `adaption_prompt` (LLaMA-Adapter): learned prompts the top attention
  layers attend to through a zero-initialised gate.
* **Scaling and selective tuning** — a small part of the model itself: `ia3` (a rescaling vector
  per layer), `ln_tuning` (a trainable copy of each chosen normalisation layer) and
  `trainable_tokens` (a few rows of an embedding table).

Twenty more methods are full tuners like the ones above, grouped by the form of their update:
`delora`, `gralora`, `hira`, `glora`, `deft` and `peanut` (a weight update of low-rank
or projection form), `unilora`, `pvera`, `tinylora` and `lily` (adapters read out of shared
banks), `road`, `psoft`, `osf` and `frod` (orthogonal and spectral updates),
`supertuning`, `waveft`, `beft` and `cartridge` (sparse, wavelet, bias and key-value
updates) and `adamss` (subspaces of the weight's SVD).  `shadow` is refused for good: its
config reads and writes, but the method needs the base model's decoder loop and a second backbone
beside it, so building it raises `NotImplementedError`.

`MixedModel` is the host of a model that holds adapters of several of these methods at once, their
layers stacked on each module; only the methods declared `mixed=True` may take part.

The modules whose names begin with an underscore here (`_base`, `_lycoris`, `_orthogonal`,
`_shared`, `_prompt` …) are the machinery the methods share, not part of the public surface.
